plan.title: chore(freshness): bind filenames embed a recoverable 32-char prefix of the session id

narratives.Description: Name `.deft/session-binds/` records by their hash alone, so a directory listing carries no fragment of a session id, and keep lookup derivable from the id.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`safeSessionFileName` kept a 32-character prefix of the session UUID in every `.deft/session-binds/<name>.json` filename. The prefix was never used for lookup, and removing it costs nothing.

Split out of #3754, which was closed as not-a-defect. What is left is hygiene, and it is cheap.

## Mechanism

`packages/core/src/freshness/bind.ts` built the record name from the first 32 characters of the session id plus a 24-hex SHA-256 slice of the full id. A UUID is 36 characters, so 4 hex characters remained unknown and the filename itself was the oracle to test them against. Measured on the issue at `0a82ac96` against a synthetic UUID: recovery succeeded in 58,946 candidates, 64.8 ms.

## Hygiene, not security

`occupancy.ts` declares cooperating local processes with Byzantine behaviour an explicit non-goal, and the #3611 decision record forbids representing occupancy as same-user authentication. The same session id is already published in `.deft/occupancy.json`, `.deft/ritual-state.json`, the bind record body, and `.deft/swarm-launch-occupancy/*.json`, so the prefix was redundant rather than dangerous. The reason to remove it is that it is gratuitous.

## The derived path is load-bearing; the prefix is not

`sessionBindPath` computes the filename from the id, and `readBoundGeneration` plus `report.ts` open that path directly -- neither ever calls `readdir`. Lookup must therefore stay derivable from the id; an opaque random name would need an index and would break O(1) resolution. The 24-hex SHA-256 slice is already deterministic and unique, so dropping the prefix and keeping the hash preserves lookup exactly.

## Existing records: tolerated, not migrated

Writes always use the hash-only name. `readBoundGeneration` falls back to the pre-rename name (`legacySessionFileName`) when the hash-only record is absent, so pins written before the rename are not orphaned and the next bind supersedes them. The fallback is a second derived path, not a scan, so lookup stays O(1).

## Coupling warning

If the JSON bodies under `.deft/` are ever tightened (say to `0600`) while prefixed bind filenames stay in place, the prefix stops being redundant and becomes independently load-bearing -- directory read permission alone would then recover an id that file permissions were meant to protect. That is a constraint on any future threat-model change, recorded in the `safeSessionFileName` docblock.

## Out of scope

- Occupancy admission semantics (#3611) and the cooperative-versus-authorization framing.
- Unbounded growth of `.deft/session-binds` -- no prune or reaper exists. Real, and separate resource hygiene.
- File permission modes on `.deft/` contents.

Refs #3117, #3754, #3611.
